atomic_obligations.prior_observation: magnetohydrodynamics on the floored lattice -- finite flow, the Alfven wave. atomic_obligations.prior_observation: ionization and the plasma state -- the plasma frequency and Debye length as proven fold quantities. Phase VII (plasma, optics, and continuous media), target one, forward from the temperature as mean throw (I-1), the ionization binding of the shell structure (III-4), Coulomb's law (EM1), and the oscillator tower (PH4b). The Debye length is the distance over which a test charge inserted into the plasma is screened by the rearrangement of the surrounding free charges: it grows with temperature, since faster electrons resist confinement in a screening cloud, and shrinks with density, since more charges screen more effectively, and beyond a few Debye lengths a charge is effectively shielded, which is what makes the plasma quasineutral on large scales. Falsification condition (the derivation stands on the One; this is only what observation would have to show to contradict it): a plasma frequency that did not rise with density, or a Debye length that did not lengthen with temperature, would break the result. External correspondence (what the derived result agrees with, never what makes it true): the measured plasma frequency and Debye screening [the plasma oscillation frequency; Debye-Huckel screening; the criteria for the plasma state]. The standard account derives the plasma frequency and Debye length from the kinetic theory of the charged gas; the framework proves them as the collective Coulomb oscillation and the screening balance. Verified: the squared plasma frequency rises with charge density, the Debye length grows with temperature and shrinks with density, and both are positive proven fold quantities; cross-checked outside.

atomic_obligations.prior_observation: the deuteron and the lightest bound states -- spin-dependence and Pauli forbid the di-nucleon. Phase V (nuclear and hadronic structure), target eight, the closing target of the phase, forward from the residual nuclear prove (V-3), Fermi statistics and Pauli exclusion (I-5), and the handedness that is the spin (D7c). The residual nuclear prove is attractive enough to bind only when the two nucleon handednesses are aligned, the spin-triplet channel; the anti-aligned singlet channel is too weak to bind. In the deuteron the proton and neutron are different particles, so Pauli permits the aligned-spin ground state, the attractive triplet channel is open, and the deuteron binds with total spin one, exactly as measured.
